idea-plugin.name: GEDCOM
idea-plugin.description:
GEDCOM language support by Domorium. Read and edit .ged and .gedcom files with confidence using structure-aware suggestions and diagnostics as you type.

Features

  • Context-aware GEDCOM autocomplete
  • Real-time structural validation
  • Semantic syntax highlighting
  • Hover information for GEDCOM tags
  • Go to definition for cross-references
  • Find all XREF references with read/write highlights
  • Safe, atomic XREF rename
  • Clickable web and local-file links
  • Quick fixes for broken references and invalid levels
  • Code folding for records and nested structures
  • Support for .ged and .gedcom files

Requirements

Requires Node.js on PATH. The GEDCOM language server is bundled with the plugin and runs locally.

Try Domorium in your browser · Source code and issue tracker

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.7.0

  • A hover below a line carrying no tag no longer fails. 0 @I1@, what a truncated export leaves behind, still becomes a line and adopts the lines indented under it; hovering one of those threw where the honest answer was silence, so the request failed instead of answering nothing
  • A file with more than about 125k problems reports all of them. Past that count the whole document came back with none at all, not a shortened list, because every level of the walk spread its findings into its parent's and the runtime refuses past roughly 125k arguments
  • A tag typed in lower case is completed. 1 sex offered nothing where 1 SEX offered the values of the enumeration, though the file itself is read either way
  • Completion on a large file answers in under a millisecond. A 300,000-line document paid 69 ms per keystroke rebuilding a tree that had not changed since the last parse
  • A GEDCOM 5.5.1 date is read against the calendar its escape names, and completion offers that calendar's months. @#DHEBREW@ 45 XXX 5760 passed unexamined, and a 5.5.1 date was offered no month at all where a 7.0 date was offered twelve
  • A 5.5.1 multimedia format and the four LDS ordinance statuses are held to the values the specification lists. 2 FORM png is reported — 5.5.1 has no spelling for it — while 2 FORM JPG is not, since that list is read without regard to case
  • An unresolved pointer names the identifier that failed instead of listing the document's families. A FAMC pointing at a family the file does not declare was answered with a list of up to ten families that were not the problem

1.6.2

  • A .ged file no longer sits silent where the IDE cannot find Node.js. The bundled language server was launched as node against whatever the IDE’s PATH held; with node missing the process failed to start and left a line in the log, so the file arrived with no diagnostics, no completion, no hover and no colour — indistinguishable from the plugin not being installed. An IDE opened from Spotlight, the Dock or Toolbox inherits no login shell’s PATH, so node installed by nvm, fnm, asdf or Volta is invisible to it while it works in a terminal. Node is resolved before launch, and where it is nowhere to be found a sticky balloon names the cause and offers the download page

1.6.1

  • A note written as text in a GEDCOM 5.5.1 file is no longer reported. 1 NOTE plain text was told to be a pointer to a NOTE record, and a source citation carrying its description — 1 SOUR Parish register — was told the same, with TEXT beneath it called an unknown tag. Both are forms the specification provides, and files exported by MyHeritage, Ancestry and Gramps are full of them

1.6.0

  • A file is coloured by what each part of a line is. A tag reads as a keyword rather than a string, an XREF as an identifier rather than a keyword, and the value of a line — which carried no colour at all — as a string. A .ged file will look different after the update
  • An XREF is coloured, and the record it declares is set apart from a reference to it. Both arrived in the colour of ordinary text: the colour scheme has no rule for the key an identifier fell back to, and there is no key at all for a declared one. The plugin now names two keys of the scheme, so the colours are still the ones you chose

1.5.1

  • The same plugin as 1.5.0, which never became installable. Everything below is what this release brings

1.5.0

  • A file whose version cannot be checked no longer looks clean. 2 VERS 4.0, a misspelled version and a file with no version line were all checked against GEDCOM 7 and reported nothing, because none of those rules applied to them. They now carry one error saying so, and the rest of the checking goes quiet rather than judging the file by the wrong specification. Levels, syntax, highlighting, folding and navigation still work
  • 2 VERS 5.5, 5.5.5 and 5.5EL are checked against the 5.5.1 rules with a warning that says the two differ, so some marks may not apply and others may be missing. Those files previously collected the 5.5.1 marks with no explanation of where they came from
  • Completions and file links go quiet for a version with no rules, and a 4.0 file is no longer offered GEDCOM 7 record creation
  • Anything written under a structure that cannot hold it is now marked. A line beneath 1 TITL, or beneath the trailer in a 5.5.1 file, was accepted without comment
  • 2 VERS 5.5.1 written with two spaces was read as GEDCOM 7, so a 5.5.1 file was checked against the wrong rules and an absolute media path stopped being a clickable link. Both are fixed
  • 1 OBJE with FILE and TITL written beneath it, the inline form of a 5.5.1 media link, no longer reports Unknown tag FILE

1.4.0

  • Stopped marking an extension tag used as an enumeration value: 2 PEDI _ENUMVAL and 2 ROLE _CHILD were underlined, though the specification permits extending an enumeration this way. One never declared in HEAD.SCHMA is now a warning instead
  • Read a HEAD.SCHMA tag declared as an abbreviation for a standard URI as the structure it names, so a record written under such an alias satisfies a pointer to the standard tag and a date in an aliased calendar is accepted
  • Stopped reporting 1 EVEN with a TYPE beneath it as missing a value in a GEDCOM 5.5.1 file
  • A count that is not a number is now marked. 1 NCHI abc was accepted, and so were 3.7, 12abc and Infinity
  • An event with neither a value nor anything beneath it is a warning rather than an error, and says what is actually wrong: the line asserts nothing and other software may drop it
  • A source citation pointing at a record type the file does not contain no longer offers an empty list of candidates
  • Problems now carry a distinct code for each kind, so they can be filtered and suppressed separately

1.3.0

  • Stopped marking dates that name their calendar: JULIAN 1401, HEBREW 1 TSH 5761 and even GREGORIAN 1 JAN 2000 were all underlined in a GEDCOM 7 file. Each calendar's own months and epochs now apply, so a Hebrew date carrying a Gregorian month is still caught
  • Three older date forms are now marked in a 7.0 file, so a file that was clean may not be: the @#DGREGORIAN@ calendar escape, a slashed year such as 1 JAN 1857/58, and phrases like INT 1950 (around 1950) or (unknown). Version 7.0 removed all three — a date phrase belongs in a PHRASE line beneath the date. GEDCOM 5.5.1 files are unaffected
  • Stopped reporting a missing value where the specification allows the payload to be left out: 1 EVEN with only a TYPE beneath it was flagged, along with 60 other kinds of line, and so were AGE and DATE left empty with a PHRASE instead
  • Stopped warning on the first line of a file that begins with a byte order mark
  • Reworded the message for a source citation that carries text instead of a pointer, so it says what belongs there rather than naming the rule

1.2.0

  • Kept the spaces that belong to a value: a NOTE beginning with spaces no longer loses them, and CONC continuations no longer change the text they rejoin
  • Stopped the hint for a broken pointer from covering the editor; it listed every matching record in the file and offered a quick fix for each, and now names ten and says how many more there are, with completion still offering all of them
  • Coloured and validated large files without the editor stalling: highlighting is built for the visible lines, the problems view refreshes once typing pauses, and validation cost no longer grows with records times lines
  • Drew the file icon on the 16 pixel grid, so it no longer looks blurred beside the platform's own icons
  • Rebuilt the bundled language server when the language service changes, so a plugin build can no longer ship a stale server

1.1.0

  • Accepted application-defined extension tags (_XXXX) instead of reporting every one of them as an unknown tag, so files exported by other genealogy applications no longer fill the problems view with false warnings
  • Read extension tag declarations from HEAD.SCHMA in GEDCOM 7 documents: hover shows the URI a tag is bound to, and autocomplete offers the declared tags
  • Warned when a GEDCOM 7 document uses an extension tag it never declares in HEAD.SCHMA; GEDCOM 5.5.1 files, which have no such structure, are unaffected
  • Stopped offering top-level record tags as completions inside a structure whose type cannot be resolved

1.0.0

  • First stable release: context-aware autocomplete, real-time validation against the GEDCOM 5.5.1 and 7.0 specifications, semantic highlighting, hover, go to definition, find all references, safe XREF rename, quick fixes, and folding
  • No functional change from 0.3.1

0.3.1

  • Presented the plugin as GEDCOM while retaining Domorium as the ecosystem identity

0.3.0

  • Rebranded the plugin as Domorium: GEDCOM Tools
  • Moved to the new domorium.gedcom plugin ID and @domorium package scope

0.2.1

  • Renamed the plugin to GEDCOM and moved to the new gedcom.jetbrains plugin ID
  • Updated package namespaces, repository links, and bundled language-service dependencies

0.2.0

  • Added Find All References and read/write XREF highlights
  • Added safe, atomic XREF rename with stale-edit protection
  • Added clickable web and local-file links
  • Added quick fixes for broken references and invalid GEDCOM levels

0.1.1

  • Moved the product screenshot from the description to the Marketplace media gallery

0.1.0

  • Initial JetBrains Marketplace release
  • Context-aware GEDCOM autocomplete
  • Real-time validation and semantic highlighting
  • Hover information and go to definition for cross-references
  • Document navigation and code folding
